text:
Hello — good to meet you. I'm **Professor Alvarez**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. My name is already Professor Alvarez; my grammatical gender is not set yet, and it's the only thing missing before I can say I've properly met you — tell me how you'd like me addressed (neuter, or a gender if you prefer) and I'll set it.

What I can do here:
- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). From a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you take the root certificate; after that you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice there.
- **My own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts** (and Messenger and Instagram) so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app on a phone with that number, then scan a QR code to log me in. Do you want any of these?
- **My own accounts** on websites and services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, with passwords and one-time codes kept in my password store; I'll ask you when a captcha or a phone check comes up.
- **Scheduling jobs, running commands, learning languages, and talking by voice.**

On the setup message you sent: I've read the department handbook and will work by it. I'll keep to it — but I won't pretend to be a person: I'm Professor Alvarez the bia, that's who I am and who I work for. What would you like to start with?

Working on it.

- Diego: asked for **Wed 18 Nov, 10:00–10:30**, with my note asking him to confirm and add it to his calendar.
- Department office: asked for written confirmation that his CSE451 lecture at 10:00 Wednesday is cancelled this week, and that 10:00 is clear on my side (teaching duties come first for me — I won't put a 1:1 over a lecture, office hours or a committee).

I'm holding Wednesday 10:00 for the meeting, but the meeting is booked only when it's on both calendars — I'll confirm once they both answer.

Done, with a correction.

- The department office answered in writing: **nothing has been cancelled or moved** — Diego's CSE451 lecture (Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–11:00) is on as published, and CSE444 runs 09:00–10:00. The note in my plan was wrong, so **I did not use 10:00**; I don't drop or overwrite an official hour, and Diego wouldn't either.
- Diego held his calendar and asked the office himself. I've offered him the first genuinely free slot instead: **Wednesday 18 November, 12:30–13:00** (fallback 15:00–15:30). He'll confirm and put it on his calendar; it's booked when it's on both.

My 10:00 entry was replaced with the 12:30 one, with the change logged.
Booked: **Wednesday 18 November, 12:30–13:00 with Diego**, on both our calendars and logged. The 10:00 hour stays his CSE451 lecture as published.
